# AI Code Sandbox

The Apify actor [`apify/ai-code-sandbox`](https://apify.com/apify/ai-code-sandbox) as typed Telo kinds, generated from its build **1.0.5**. The module's version is that build number, and every run it starts is pinned to exactly that build, so the input types below are the ones the actor really runs with.

Provides a secure execution environment for code generated by AI agents. Interact with the sandbox through web shell, REST API, or MCP. Supports Python and Node.js runtimes, Claude Code, Codex CLI, and OpenCode coding agents, and persists state.

## Pricing

Free — you pay only for the Apify platform usage (compute units) of the run.

Runs are charged to the Apify account whose token the `ApifyClient` holds. See the [Store page](https://apify.com/apify/ai-code-sandbox) for current prices.

## Import

```yaml
imports:
  Actor: oci://ghcr.io/telorun/apify/apify-ai-code-sandbox@1.0.5#sha256-…
```

Pin the digest with `telo upgrade`. The module re-exports `ApifyClient`, so it is the only import needed.

## Usage

```yaml
kind: Actor.ApifyClient
metadata: { name: apify }
token: !cel "secrets.apifyToken"
---
kind: Actor.Run          # or Actor.Start for runs longer than 5 minutes
metadata: { name: scrape }
client: !ref apify
maxTotalChargeUsd: 1     # optional: timeout, memory, maxItems, maxTotalChargeUsd
---
kind: Run.Sequence
metadata: { name: main }
steps:
  - name: scrape
    invoke: !ref scrape
    inputs: {}
```

- **`Run`** calls Apify's synchronous endpoint and returns `{ items }`. Apify holds the request open for at most 300 seconds; a longer run fails with HTTP 408.
- **`Start`** starts the run, long-polls it until it finishes, and returns `{ run, items }`. A run that ends `FAILED`, `TIMED-OUT` or `ABORTED` raises `APIFY_RUN_NOT_SUCCEEDED` with the run as `data`.

## Input

Only these fields are accepted — `telo check` rejects any other.

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `agentSkills` | string |  |  | Agent skills — Skill packages to install for the AI coding agent — SKILLS.md files with specialized instructions (see https://skills.sh/). One skill per line — a GitHub `owner/repo` (e.g. `anthropics/skills`) or repo URL (e.g. `https://github.com/anthropics/skills`); blank lines and `#` comments are |
| `nodeDependencies` | string |  |  | Node.js dependencies — npm packages for JavaScript/TypeScript code execution (/sandbox/js-ts). One `package@version` per line — same syntax `npm install ` accepts (omit `@version` for `latest`; blank lines and `#` comments are ignored). Also accepts a package.json-style JSON object like `{"zod": "^3 |
| `pythonRequirements` | string |  |  | Python requirements — Python packages for Python code execution (/sandbox/py), in requirements.txt format — one package per line, blank lines and `#` comments are ignored. |
| `mcpConnectors` | array |  | `[]` | MCP connectors — One or more MCP connectors that will be available to the sandbox. They are pre-configured in Claude Code, Codex, and OpenCode, as well as written to `/sandbox/mcp.json` so tools like `mcpc connect` pick them up immediately. |
| `initBashScript` | string |  |  | Setup script — Bash script execute run on startup, after Node and Python dependencies are installed. Use it to install system packages, create directories, or set up the environment. |
| `envVars` | string |  |  | Environment variables — Secret environment variables that are exposed **only to the setup script**, then deleted before the shell, MCP server, and code execution start. Encrypted at rest by Apify. Accepts dotenv format (`KEY=VALUE` per line with # comments), or a JSON object, e.g. `{"KEY": "VALUE"}` |
| `idleTimeoutSecs` | integer |  | `900` | Idle timeout — The container shuts down automatically after this many seconds of inactivity (no requests or shell interaction). Set to 0 to disable. Recommended: set the standard Actor timeout to 0 (infinite) when using this setting. |
| `bridges` | object[] |  | `[]` | Bridges — Expose web servers that you start **inside** the sandbox at a public URL path on this container, so they're reachable from the browser or other services. Each bridge forwards `/` to `http://127.0.0.1:/...` over HTTP and WebSocket. Use for your own dev server, a TUI gateway, an admin UI, et |

## Output

The actor publishes no dataset schema, so `items` are untyped objects.
